newsitem.title: POLAND: Political row flares in Poland over Russian agents.
newsitem.headline: Political row flares in Poland over Russian agents.

text.p: A political row has erupted in Poland over an accusation by the country's security minister that Russian secret services have stepped up activity to try to block Warsaw's entry into the European Union and NATO.

Just before leaving for talks with German intelligence chiefs, Security Minister Zbigniew Siemiatkowski repeated his charge against Moscow originally contained in a Saturday newspaper interview, PAP news agency said.
He said Russian intelligence agents were trying to create a pro-Russian lobby to block Warsaw's entry into the two Western institutions, the agency said.

Semiatkowski first made the charge in remarks published on Saturday in the heavyweight daily Rzeczpospolita, saying Polish counter-intelligence had noticed increased contacts by Russian diplomats with Polish politicians.
He added the contacts were both with officials from the ruling coalition of the post-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and Peasant Party (PSL) as well as with the opposition.
The opposition centrist Freedom Union party (UW) on Sunday demanded that Siemiatkowski explain his remarks before parliament.

"Sensations are usually the stock in trade of journalists, not ministers," PAP reported UW parliamentary leader Bronislaw Geremek as saying. He added that Siemiatkowski had not backed up his remarks with any evidence.
Janusz Piechocinski of the SLD's junior coalition partner PSL said in a radio discussion on Sunday that Siemiatkowski's statements could harm Poland's international interests.
Siemiatkowski's words also prompted the right-wing Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) to demand the sacking of all public officials and activists with links to Russian special services.
